newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slide but market upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slide but market upbeat.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped again on Monday but market sentiment seemed to perk up after recent doldrums on an announcement that international securities house ING Barings was setting up shop in Cairo.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index slipped for the fourth day running by 0.71 points to 350.81 points but brokers said the market reacted positively to news that London-based ING Barings would take a share in a new Cairo brokerage in partnership with local companies.
Turnover was a below-average 43.54 million pounds ($12.82 million).
"It (announcement) has added confidence to the market. These huge firms will not set up a brokerage unless they felt secure. Others are going to join them soon," corporate sources said.

Local brokers Intercapital will manage the new firm whose Egyptian partners include Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), the investment affiliate of Commercial International Bank (CIB), and Mansour and Maghraby, an investment group with diverse interests.
Last year, securities house HSBC James Capel said they too were setting up shop in Cairo.
Broker Mohammed Abdallah of Intercapital also attributed the cheerier mood to price gains in CIB stock, whose 1996 dividend sent share prices tumbling and the market lower.
CIB disappointed shareholders when it announced on Thursday it would give a 2.00 pound dividend, but on Monday the share ended 2.00 pounds higher at 66.9 pounds.

"Whoever is buying CIB now is the educated investor. CIB made a very smart move by increasing its reserves as opposed to giving higher payouts as this will strengthen its balance sheet for everyone abroad," Abdallah said.

Another active share was North Cairo Flour Mills which rose 3.5 to 165 pounds, bucking a downtrend which struck the popular state-dominated milling sector last week after brokers said private mills were going to be stiff competition for the state.

Cement shares also attracted investors with Egyptian Portland Tora Cement taking the lion's share of the Monday's trade but shares fell 0.65 to 87.25 pounds. Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA was also busy and rose 0.05 to 70.41.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 487.82 points from 483.81 points on Sunday and that for the rarely-traded "closed" firms slipped to 257.46 points from 259.32.
Out of 88 shares traded, 51 rose and 10 fell while 27 ended unchanged.
